adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The inverted substring check lets refresh-grant access-token IDs pass authorization-code assertions, hiding incorrect grant context.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — A custom grant using the documented three-character shortcut produces token IDs that this decoder always rejects.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that three-character shortcuts would be rejected, but the diff shows the decoder expects exactly 6 characters for the encoded context (line 74: 'if (encodedContext.length() != 6)'). The format is: 2 chars for sessionType + 2 chars for tokenType + 2 chars for grantType = 6 chars total. All grant shortcuts in the diff are 2 characters (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', etc.), not 3. The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc mentions '3-letters shortcut' but all actual implementations use 2-character shortcuts. The decoder correctly handles 2-character shortcuts, not 3-character ones as the finding suggests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding required getShortcut() breaks existing grant-provider binaries because startup invokes it unconditionally and fails with AbstractMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface (in server-spi-private) adds a new abstract method `getShortcut()` without a default implementation. This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that haven't been updated. When Keycloak starts, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls getShortcut() on each one. If an external/custom grant type provider exists that was compiled against the old interface (without getShortcut()), calling this method will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime. The finding correctly identifies this as a binary compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — The decoder rejects three-character grant shortcuts permitted by the new factory contract, so tokens encoded for compliant custom grants cannot round-trip.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the decoder rejects three-character grant shortcuts, but examining the code shows: 1) The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() method has no documented constraint on length - it just says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. 2) Looking at all the factory implementations in the diff, ALL shortcuts are exactly 2 characters (ac, cc, pg, pc, rt, ro, te, ci, dg). 3) The decoder at line 74 checks 'encodedContext.length() != 6' which expects exactly 6 characters total (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType). This is consistent with all the 2-character shortcuts defined. The finding incorrectly states that 3-character shortcuts are 'permitted by the new factory contract' when in fact all implementations use 2-character shortcuts and the decoder expects 2-character shortcuts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 — The SPI permits arbitrary shortcut lengths while the decoder hard-codes two characters, so compliant grant providers can emit token IDs the framework cannot decode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as returning 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' with no length enforcement. However, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() at line 72-80 hard-codes parsing logic expecting exactly 6 characters for the encoded context (2 chars each for sessionType, tokenType, grantType). If a grant provider returns a shortcut that is not exactly 2 characters, the encoding/decoding will fail or produce incorrect results. The interface allows arbitrary lengths while the implementation assumes fixed 2-character shortcuts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — The lazy registration path overwrites both inverse maps without duplicate-shortcut validation, so a late grant can change how already-issued IDs decode.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java, the postInit method (lines 63-82) validates that there are no duplicate shortcuts by checking if grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(). However, in getShortcutByGrantType (lines 103-117) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 119-135), when a new grant type is discovered at runtime, the code simply puts the new mappings into both maps without checking for duplicate shortcuts. If a late-deployed grant has the same shortcut as an existing one, it would overwrite the existing mapping, causing already-issued token IDs to decode incorrectly. This is a real correctness bug - the lazy registration bypasses the duplicate validation that exists in postInit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId checks the wrong slice and rejects matches, so the shared matcher does not enforce the expected grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the isAccessTokenId matcher. Looking at the code: `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts characters at indices 3-4 (2 chars), but the format shown in tests like 'trltcc:1234' has the grant shortcut at positions 4-5 (0-indexed: 'tr'=0-1, 'lt'=2-3, 'cc'=4-5). So substring(3,5) gets 'tc' instead of 'cc'. Additionally, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when they ARE equal, which is backwards logic - it should return false when they DON'T match. This is a real bug that would cause the matcher to reject valid token IDs and accept invalid ones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Grant shortcuts are accepted without enforcing the decoder's two-character format, so a custom grant can issue token IDs that later cannot be decoded.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. Looking at the diff, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java collects grant shortcuts from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations (lines 68-73) without validating that shortcuts are exactly 2 characters. The decoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() (lines 69-71) expects exactly 6 characters for encodedContext and parses it as 2+2+2 character segments. If a custom grant provides a shortcut that isn't exactly 2 characters, the encoding would produce token IDs that cannot be properly decoded. The factory only validates that maps have same size (no duplicate shortcuts/grants), but doesn't validate the 2-character format requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The access-token matcher checks the wrong substring and rejects equality, so integration tests pass even when the encoded grant shortcut is wrong.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in line 483: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` - This returns false when the grant shortcut MATCHES, which is backwards logic. The matcher should return true when the shortcut matches and false when it doesn't. Additionally, the substring indices are wrong - the comment says 'starts at character 4th char' but substring(3, 5) extracts characters at indices 3-4 (2 chars starting at 4th position, 0-indexed). Looking at the token format like 'onrtna:5678', the grant shortcut is at positions 4-5 (indices 4-5), so substring(4, 6) would be correct. The combination of wrong indices and inverted logic means tests will pass incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — isAccessTokenId slices the wrong prefix characters and rejects equality, so integration tests accept token IDs carrying the wrong grant context.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the isAccessTokenId method in the diff (lines 476-489), the code does `items[0].substring(3, 5)` to extract the grant shortcut. However, based on the token format shown in encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java), the format is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort(2) + ':' + rawTokenId`. So the grant shortcut is at positions 4-6 (0-indexed: characters 4 and 5), meaning substring should be `substring(4, 6)` not `substring(3, 5)`. Additionally, the condition uses `equals()` with negation - `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` - which returns false when the grant MATCHES, which is backwards logic. It should return false when it does NOT match. This is a real bug that would cause tests to incorrectly pass/fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:82 — testIncorrectGrantType catches the NullPointerException from its uninitialized sessionFactory, so it passes without exercising the intended invalid-grant rejection.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the test code in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, the @Before method creates a factory but never sets factory.sessionFactory (it's left null). The test testIncorrectGrantType() calls provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId('ofrtac:5678') which should fail because 'ac' is not in the grantsByShortcuts map. Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(), when getGrantTypeByShortcut returns null, it throws IllegalArgumentException. However, getGrantTypeByShortcut in the factory first checks grantsByShortcuts, and if null, tries to access sessionFactory which is null. Since 'ac' is not in grantsByShortcuts, it will try to access the null sessionFactory, causing NullPointerException instead of the intended IllegalArgumentException. The test catches RuntimeException (parent of both), so it passes but for the wrong reason - it's not testing the intended grant type validation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:45 — No test asserts session and token classification from getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, so regressions in online, offline, transient, regular, or lightweight encoding remain invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new method `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java (lines 45-62) that contains non-trivial logic for classifying session types (TRANSIENT, OFFLINE, ONLINE) and token types (LIGHTWEIGHT, REGULAR). The test file `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java` only tests `getTokenContextFromTokenId` and `encodeTokenId` methods - it does not test `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`. This is a valid concern since the classification logic could have bugs that wouldn't be caught. The finding correctly identifies that this new business logic lacks test coverage.
